input.summary:
Build a compact desk air monitor. It measures temperature, humidity and real CO2 (no estimate). A 0.96 in OLED shows the values. The device serves its own web page over home Wi-Fi, with a day of history kept in memory, so there is no account and no cloud. It runs on USB-C power.

Hardware: ESP32-C3 module on a custom KiCad board, made by a fab such as JLCPCB. Sensor: the team picks a true CO2 sensor (likely Sensirion SCD4x, which also gives temperature and humidity). Case: 3D printed on your printer.

Done means: KiCad project with fab files and parts list, firmware source, printable case files, and a short build and test guide. You order, solder, print, flash and test.

Left out: battery, cloud, phone app, history that survives a restart.

Notes: a day of history is kept in RAM, so it is lost on restart or power loss. The phone only reaches the page on your home Wi-Fi. Wi-Fi name and password are set in a config file you edit.

members.name: Hardware engineer
members.responsibility: Choose the parts, design the schematic and the KiCad board, and prepare the fab files and parts list.
members.reason: The custom board is the core of the project.

members.name: Firmware engineer
members.responsibility: Write the ESP32-C3 firmware: sensor reading, OLED display, Wi-Fi, and the web page with a day of history.
members.reason: The device needs software for the display and the web page.

members.name: Mechanical designer
members.responsibility: Design the printable case with files your slicer can open, to fit the board and screen.
members.reason: The case must fit the board and be printable at home.

tasks.title: Choose the CO2 sensor and main parts
tasks.description: A short parts list with the true CO2 sensor, ESP32-C3 module, OLED, USB-C connector, power regulator, and reasons, price and stock check notes. Done when the manager can read it and see total cost.

tasks.title: Approve the parts choice
tasks.description: Read the parts list and approve or change it before design starts.

tasks.title: Define the pin map
tasks.description: A document listing which ESP32-C3 pin connects to the sensor, OLED, and any button or LED, with I2C addresses and power rails. Done when firmware and board can both work from it.

tasks.title: Draw the schematic
tasks.description: KiCad schematic with USB-C power, regulator, ESP32-C3 with boot and reset circuit, sensor, OLED connection. Electrical rules check passes.

tasks.title: Lay out the board
tasks.description: Compact KiCad board layout that follows the fab's rules, with the sensor kept away from heat sources and the antenna clear. Design rules check passes.

tasks.title: Define the board and mounting dimensions
tasks.description: A document with board outline, hole positions, USB-C position, OLED window position and sensor opening and part heights. Done when the case can be drawn from it.

tasks.title: Prepare fab files and parts list
tasks.description: Gerber, drill, bill of materials and part position files for JLCPCB, plus a short order guide. Done when the files match the final layout.

tasks.title: Order the board and parts
tasks.description: Place the fab and parts orders and wait for delivery.

tasks.title: Write the sensor and display code
tasks.description: Firmware that reads CO2, temperature and humidity every few seconds and shows them on the OLED. Written from the pin map and ready to build.

tasks.title: Write the Wi-Fi and history code
tasks.description: Firmware that joins Wi-Fi from a config file and keeps a day of readings in memory, sized to fit the chip's RAM.

tasks.title: Write the phone web page
tasks.description: A web page served by the device with current values and a history chart, readable on a phone, with no outside files needed.

tasks.title: Write the build and flash guide
tasks.description: A short guide for building the firmware, setting Wi-Fi details, flashing over USB, and finding the page address.

tasks.title: Design the case
tasks.description: Printable case in STL files, with OLED window, USB-C opening and air vents for the sensor. Fits the dimensions document.

tasks.title: Print the case and check the fit
tasks.description: Print the case, test it with the real board, and report any fit problems.

tasks.title: Solder, flash and test the device
tasks.description: Solder the board, flash the firmware, check the readings against an outdoor or known value, and report faults.

tasks.title: Write the bring-up checklist and test guide
tasks.description: A step-by-step list for first power-up: voltage checks, what to expect, and common faults, so the manager can debug.

content.text: I proposed a team of three: a hardware engineer, a firmware engineer and a mechanical designer. The plan has 16 tasks, from choosing the CO2 sensor through the KiCad board, firmware, web page and case. Ordering, soldering, printing and testing are yours.
